title: Displacing Hegemonic Psychology Through Dissidence: Dialogues Between Cultural Psychology, Decolonial Epistemologies, and the Go-Along Method
abstract: This article offers a theoretical and methodological contribution to Psychology through an articulation between the Cultural Psychology of semiotic dynamics and decolonial epistemologies. We interrogate hegemonic configurations and their complicity with modern-colonial logics, the universalization of US-Eurocentric models of subjectivity, and the marginalization of relational, sociocultural, and historically situated dimensions of human psychological processes. Drawing on the concepts of fractured locus (María Lugones) and nepantla (Gloria Anzaldúa), we approach dissidence as a site of rupture and traversal within dominant regimes of intelligibility, where insurgent modes of meaning-making emerge from lives positioned at the borders of normative orders. Dissident life trajectories operate as epistemic forces that can strain established frameworks of recognition and open possibilities for alternative ways of inquiring, knowing, and relating across lived territories. The article articulates the go-along method through Ignacio Martín-Baró’s notion of contact, conceptualizing it as an ethically implicated practice of inquiry grounded in embodied co-presence, relational accountability, and movement across memory-laden territories. Selected episodes from three non-binary developmental trajectories illustrate the methodological possibilities and ethical tensions of this approach. By foregrounding dissident phenomena as generating epistemic displacements, the article contributes to the ongoing reinvention of Psychology as a situated, relational, and ethically implicated practice.
authors: Maria Claudia Santos Lopes de Oliveira
